product_one_liner.value: iVoyant’s Koodisi is an enterprise integration platform that lets IT, integration and operations teams connect business systems and automate workflows without code, with built-in API management.

pricing_page.notes: The public page describes one enterprise plan with quote-based pricing rather than published dollar amounts.

named_customers.notes: The capability statement identifies projects delivered for both companies.

employee_band.notes: Company-size band reported on its LinkedIn page.

eng_blog.notes: Includes engineer-authored implementation posts by Carlos Gutierrez on a Firebase application and Ayush Sharma on the internal PlatformNX copilot architecture.

public_docs.notes: Public documentation includes multiple user guides, activity documentation and release notes.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: A live AI/ML Engineer posting in Bangalore includes an application option.

model_provider.notes: Product documentation, security/privacy pages and the technical blog do not explicitly identify a model provider used by the product; general model examples and job-skill requirements do not establish product usage.

compliance_certs.notes: SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are described as approved, but their certificates remain in the issuing pipeline and have not been issued; excluded as incomplete.

last_funding.notes: The company profile reports no funding rounds.

raised_18mo.notes: The funding profile reports that iVoyant has not raised any funding rounds.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The current board lists five engineering/design roles and no SDR, BDR or account executive role.

launched_6mo.notes: The October 2026 release introduced Agent Studio (Beta) and Koodisi AI workflow building, deployment and testing from chat.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: The four-person team page was reviewed in full and no recent C-level/VP appointment or departure was found. This is an absence-based result; the page does not provide start dates.

crm_stack_signal.notes: Both are named in a historical, now-closed SDR posting; these are hiring-based stack signals, not confirmation of current deployment.
